# Routing judge requests — live fixtures

Each `A-00N.request.json` is the exact `{ state, questions }` that `routingRequest()` in `mcp/jev/routing.ts` (question_version `2026-09-23.2`) built for the real assignment `sb-dogfood-3/r1/A-00N`, with the three lanes the run registry held at the A-005 re-measurement (w1 `skill-doc-lines`/default, w2 `merge-audit`/slow, w3 `assignment-routing`/task) and the `delegation.md` sections as they stood on 2026-09-23. Generated by a throwaway script from the run's canonical artifacts; not hand-edited.

`state.assignment` carries only `goal` and `completion_conditions` — the frontmatter answers (`profile`, `responsibility_key`) are deliberately absent. `state.delegation_rules` is the `## Three routes` and `## Profile selection` text; `state.lanes` is the registry projection.

Live verdicts (jev-1.13.0) recorded in the run's `plan.md` D-15 (v1) and D-23 (v2), for comparison against any redesign:

| assignment | dispatched as | route v1 (`2026-09-23.1`) | route v2 (`2026-09-23.2`) | profile v2 | reuse v2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-001 | lane, default | undecided (host 0.54 / lane 0.46) | undecided (orch 0.49 / lane 0.45 / host 0.06) | default 0.78 | lane:skill-doc-lines 0.99 |
| A-002 | lane, slow | undecided (lane 0.43 / orch 0.36 / host 0.21) | orch-self 0.79 | slow 1.00 | lane:merge-audit 0.98 |
| A-003 | lane, default | — | orch-self 0.82 | task 0.81 (disagrees) | lane:skill-doc-lines 0.93 |
| A-004 | lane, task | — | orch-self 0.85 | task 0.99 | lane:assignment-routing 0.75 |

Every route answer is wrong or undecided against the actual dispatch; profile and reuse hold. The known defects, from the ORCH's reading: the `route` criteria are pointers ("The Yourself route in delegation_rules.") rather than the row text itself, unlike `profile` whose criteria carry the table's intent cells verbatim; and the first row of the Three routes table names decisions, assignments and `plan.md`, vocabulary every assignment goal contains.

## v3 (`2026-09-23.3`) — whole `delegation.md` unedited, assignment = goal only

`A-00N.request.v3.json` / `A-00N.verdict.v3.json`, measured live on 2026-09-23 with the same lanes.

| assignment | dispatched as | route v3 | profile v3 | reuse v3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-001 | lane, default | orch-self 0.60 (conf 0.40; lane 0.34 / host 0.06) | default 0.84 | lane:skill-doc-lines 0.98 |
| A-002 | lane, slow | orch-self 0.88 (conf 0.82) | slow 0.97 | lane:merge-audit 0.84 |
| A-003 | lane, default | orch-self 0.85 (conf 0.77) | undecided (conf 0.27) | lane:skill-doc-lines 0.90 |
| A-004 | lane, task | orch-self 0.87 (conf 0.80) | task 0.95 | lane:assignment-routing 0.80 |

Route is now uniformly `orch-self`, more confident than v2, and still wrong for all four. Giving the judge the whole document and only the goal did not move the answer toward the actual dispatch; the goal prose alone reads as ORCH-language work to it.

## v4 experiment — `experiment-v4.json`

Same four artifacts and lanes, route question only, one live call per cell (jev-1.13.0). Correct = the actual dispatch (all four went to a lane).

| variant | A-001 | A-002 | A-003 | A-004 | correct |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v3 whole doc + goal (baseline) | undecided | orch-self | orch-self | orch-self | 0/4 |
| v4a + `definitions` | lane 0.63 | orch-self 0.95 | orch-self 0.68 | orch-self 0.67 | 1/4 |
| v4b + definitions + write_ownership/user_boundaries/dependencies | lane 0.68 | orch-self 0.91 | undecided | orch-self 0.64 | 1/4 |
| v4c + definitions + fields, criteria = paraphrased row text | lane 1.00 | orch-self 0.63 | lane 1.00 | lane 0.99 | 3/4 |
| v4d definitions + fields, **no rules doc**, criteria paraphrased | lane 1.00 | lane 0.60 | lane 1.00 | lane 0.99 | 4/4 |
| v4e + definitions + fields, criteria = **verbatim** table rows | lane 0.97 | orch-self 0.71 | lane 1.00 | lane 0.98 | 3/4 |

`definitions` (in the file) say what an assignment is — a document the ORCH writes for a worker, author not executor — and what each route means. That single addition is what moves the judge off `orch-self`; inlining the row text as criteria is what makes it confident. A-002 (the slow-lane merge audit) is the residual: with the rules document present the judge reads "a decision / a rejected alternative" in row 1 and keeps it for the ORCH; without the document (v4d) it goes to a lane at 0.60. Whether an audit that feeds a user decision is ORCH work or a slow lane's is a judgment the document itself leaves to the ORCH.

## v5 (`2026-09-23.4`) — adopted

Question reworded from a table lookup to a suitability judgment ("Which executor is the most suitable to achieve this assignment's goal…", with the note that an existing assignment means `orch-self` = "should not have been written"); criteria = the Signal cells of the Three routes table verbatim, grouped per route; state = whole `delegation.md` unedited + `assignment{goal, write_ownership, user_boundaries, dependencies}` + lanes. No `definitions`: `experiment-v5-nodef.json` shows 7/7 without them (A-001 0.95, A-002 0.81, A-003 0.99, A-004 0.98; synthetic F-orch 0.99 orch-self, F-sub 1.00 host-subagent, F-lane 1.00 lane). `experiment-v5-fakes.json` holds the three synthetic goals.
